conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good evening. I'm Dr. Lee, one of the surgical team. You're here because of abdominal pain and not passing gas. Can you tell me more about what’s been going on?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, the pain started about 12 hours ago. It feels like my old blockages. I haven’t passed flatus since this morning. I’ve been having these episodes for years because of my sclerosing mesenteritis.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I see. And you mentioned forgetfulness yesterday—has that improved?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, that’s gone now. It scared me, but it only lasted a few hours.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Okay, good. We reviewed your CT scans from earlier today. There’s no sign of a complete bowel obstruction, but your G-tube appears blocked. We’ll place an NG tube temporarily to help decompress your stomach.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Will that hurt? I’ve had NG tubes before—they’re uncomfortable.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It can be uncomfortable, but we’ll guide it gently through your nose. We’ll also give you something to help with the discomfort. It’s temporary—just until we fix the G-tube issue.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, I trust you. What about my G-tube? It’s been acting up since I stopped venting it at home.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s likely why it’s clogged. Thick mucus built up. We’ll clean it out and may need to replace and upsize it so it doesn’t happen again. That’s planned for later in the week.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ve had so many surgeries… I just want this managed without another big operation.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re not planning surgery. This is a minor procedure with radiology. You’ll be sedated, and they’ll replace the tube using imaging to guide it. Very low risk.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That sounds better. Thank you.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. How are you feeling? The NG tube is working—your stomach is decompressing.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: The pain is a bit better, but I hate this tube. When can we remove it?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Once your G-tube is replaced and working well. We’re scheduling that for Thursday. In the meantime, we’re keeping you NPO—no food or drink by mouth.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: No food? How will I get nutrition?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll give you IV fluids and electrolytes. Since you’re off TPN now, we’re not restarting it unless needed. Your body just needs a rest right now.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay. And my other meds? I take gabapentin, lamotrigine, and aripiprazole.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ve restarted those. You’re getting them through the IV or crushed, since you can’t swallow pills right now. We’re monitoring for any side effects.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your labs came back. Your white count is normal, no sign of infection. But your hemoglobin is low—9.2—and your bicarbonate is a bit low, suggesting mild metabolic acidosis. We’ll keep an eye on it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Is that serious? I’ve always been anemic.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It’s consistent with your history of chronic disease. We’re not transfusing—you’re stable. But we’ll make sure you’re getting enough iron and nutrients when you start eating again.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: How’s the pain today? Still managing okay with the Dilaudid?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, the pain is much better. I don’t need it as often. Can I try sipping water?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Not yet. We want to wait until after your G-tube is replaced. We don’t want to risk worsening the obstruction.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Makes sense. I just miss normal routines.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good news—your G-tube replacement is scheduled for tomorrow morning. The radiology team will upsize it to reduce future clogs.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’m a little nervous. Will I be awake?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ll get light sedation—fentanyl and midazolam—so you’ll be relaxed and won’t feel pain. Someone will monitor your vitals the whole time.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, that helps. And after? When can I eat?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll start with a liquid diet the next day if all goes well. We’ll also begin a new medication called methylnaltrexone to help with bowel motility.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: What does that do?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It helps stimulate your bowels without affecting pain control. It’s especially useful for people on narcotics who have slow motility.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hi, you just came back from the procedure. It went perfectly. Your G-tube was upsized to 16 French and is working well. You tolerated sedation without issues.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I feel groggy, but okay. Is the old tube gone?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, replaced and confirmed in the right spot with imaging. We’ll remove the NG tube later today once we see the G-tube is venting properly.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: The G-tube is draining well. We’ve removed the NG tube. You can start small sips of water now.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you! That’s a relief. Can I have broth tomorrow?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: If you tolerate water, we’ll advance to clear liquids tomorrow. We’re making good progress.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re doing well. We got your urine culture back—it shows Klebsiella pneumoniae, but you’re not running a fever or having symptoms. We don’t think you need antibiotics.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Is that a UTI? I’ve had those before.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Possibly, but since you’re not symptomatic, we’ll just monitor. Treating it without symptoms could lead to resistance. We’ll check again if you develop fever or pain.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, that makes sense.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re now on full liquids and your bowels are moving. We’re going to switch your pain meds to Dilaudid suppositories as needed. You said you have some at home?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, I have a few left. I’ll use them sparingly.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good. We’re also sending you home on methylnaltrexone to keep your motility improved. And ranitidine for reflux.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Will I need another follow-up with GI?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, in two weeks with Dr. Evans. They’ll assess your G-tube care and overall bowel function. We want to prevent future blockages.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ve done great. We’re planning to discharge you tomorrow. You’re tolerating food, pain is minimal, and your G-tube is working.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’m ready to go home. What should I watch for?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Call us if you have severe pain, can’t pass gas, or develop a fever over 101. Also, make sure to vent your G-tube regularly to avoid mucus buildup.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my meds? I take a lot.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ll continue all your home meds: gabapentin, lamotrigine, aripiprazole, and the new ones—ranitidine and methylnaltrexone. We’re not giving a new Dilaudid script since you have suppositories at home.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: What about driving?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Not until you’re off pain meds. Even then, go slow. You might feel weak or tired for a few weeks.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: The physical therapist saw you today. You’re strong enough to go home with visiting nursing services to help with G-tube care.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s a relief. I was worried about managing alone.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. Your discharge orders are ready. You’re going home today. We’ll review everything with you before you leave.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you so much. I feel much better.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. Remember: vent your G-tube daily, take your meds, and follow up in two weeks. Call us if anything changes.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. I’ve learned my lesson—no skipping G-tube care!

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Exactly. That’s the best way to avoid another hospital stay. Take care.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you, Doctor.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Nurse will be in with your discharge paperwork and prescriptions shortly.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Got it. I’m ready.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: One last thing—your urine culture showed Klebsiella, but since you’re not symptomatic, no treatment is needed. Just monitor for burning or urgency.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Will do. I’ll keep an eye on it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: And if you have migraines or asthma flares, use your usual rescue meds. You’re cleared for light activity, but avoid heavy lifting for six weeks.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ll take it easy. Thank you for explaining everything so clearly.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re very welcome. We’re glad you’re feeling better. Have a safe trip home.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I appreciate all the care.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Take care of yourself. Call us with any concerns.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. Goodbye for now.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Goodbye.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: See you at follow-up.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Looking forward to it. Rest well.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Nurse will assist you with discharge soon.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, I’m ready when they are.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Have a smooth recovery.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. Thanks again.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. Take care.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Bye.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Goodbye.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: See you soon.
